title: Rapid Recovery Decision Lattice and SLO Triage Runbook
author: Marina Patel
content:
Summary

This runbook defines a rapid-recovery decision lattice for oncall SREs to triage SLO violations, apply error-budget-aware mitigations, and drive short-term capacity actions while preserving long-term reliability. It is intended for use during incidents with user-visible latency/availability impact and during scheduled SLO breach drills. The document links triage decisions to concrete mitigation playbooks, observability queries, and tooling commands to reduce cognitive load under pressure.

Scope

- Services: API gateway, inference-router, serving-runtime (all public model-serving endpoints).
- Incident types: P99 latency regression, 5xx availability degradation, sustained elevated token cost due to routing storms.
- Exclusions: non-production experimental clusters, batch/analytics-only pipelines.

Definitions

- SLO (Service Level Objective): Target measurable for a service (e.g., availability 99.95% over 30 days; P99 latency < 200ms for short-sequence requests).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO. Tracked per-service and per-tenant where applicable.
- Decision lattice: A prioritized graph of mitigation decisions, ranked by risk and impact on error budget and customer experience.

Decision Lattice (high level)

1) Fast mitigation (local, reversible, low-cost)
   - Prefix KV cache warm-up (cache-hint request)
   - Reduce model temperature/compute-intensive knobs for inference-heavy routes (runtime flag switch)
   - Increase short-term autoscale target by +1 replica for GPU pools tagged burst-capable

2) Medium mitigation (requires coordination or short downtime)
   - Canary rollback to previous model version (route weight -> previous version)
   - Route heavy tenants to cheaper, higher-throughput model variant (policy-based routing)
   - Temporarily disable non-critical telemetry or background tasks that consume GPU cycles

3) Conservative mitigation (major cost or potential data-exposure tradeoffs)
   - Enable degraded quality mode (aggressive quantization profiles)
   - Reroute traffic to dedicated capacity pools (billing/contract implications)
   - Initiate customer-facing throttles / rate-limits with comms plan

Decision lattice guidance: Always prefer lower-tier mitigations first unless telemetry indicates catastrophic failure (e.g., control plane unreachable, storage corruption). Document chosen mitigation in incident timeline and update error-budget ledger.

Runbook: Rapid Recovery (step-by-step)

1) Initial evidence collection (0-5 minutes)
   - Confirm the alert: check alert details in PagerDuty and the alerting dashboard.
   - Run the standard SLO query:
     - Observability: "query: slo_rollup(service=serving-runtime, window=30d)" in the SLO dashboard.
     - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, KV cache hit-rate.
   - Snapshot logs: run
     - `rbx-telemetry snapshot --service serving-runtime --since 5m --out /tmp/incident-snap.json`

2) Rapid hypothesis (5-10 minutes)
   - Use the triage checklist:
     - Is the increase in latency correlated with CPU/GPU saturation?
     - Is there a model rollout or configuration change in the last 30 minutes?
     - Is the issue isolated to a region/availability zone or global?
   - Assign preliminary owner (oncall SRE + service owner).

3) Apply fast mitigations (10-25 minutes)
   - If GPU utilization > 85% and queue_depth > 200: trigger autoscale bump (fast path):
     - `infractl autoscale apply --pool serving-gpu --delta +1 --reason "incident: autoscale-bump"`
   - If P99 latency > SLO and KV cache hit-rate < 40%: apply cache warm-up for top 20 prefixes:
     - `servingctl cache-warm --service serving-runtime --prefix-file top-prefixes.txt`
   - If change detected in last 30m: rollback rollout weights to previous stable model:
     - `routerctl traffic-split set --service serving-runtime --model v2 --weight 0 --model v1 --weight 100`

4) Monitor and decide (25-45 minutes)
   - If mitigations restore SLOs: continue monitoring for 1 hour and prepare a short post-incident note.
   - If partial improvement: escalate to medium mitigations and open an incident bridge.
   - If no improvement: engage service product manager and platform infra for conservative mitigations.

Capacity Signals and Thresholds (operational thresholds)

- Immediate signals (automated alert triggers):
  - GPU pool average utilization > 85% for 5m
  - Per-region P99 latency exceeds SLO by 30% for 10m
  - 5xx rate > 1% of requests for 5m (for critical lanes)
  - Error budget burn rate > 3x projected for the remainder of the period

- Escalation thresholds:
  - Error budget consumed > 50% within 7 days -> schedule capacity review within 24 hours.
  - Error budget exhausted -> initiate Priority-1 runbook; suspend non-essential deployments and open capacity procurement channel.

Error Budget Triage Matrix (quick reference table)

| Error Budget Remaining | Burn Rate | Recommended Action | Timebox |
|------------------------|-----------|--------------------|--------|
| > 50%                 | < 2x      | Normal ops, watch  | 4 hours|
| 20–50%                | 2–4x      | Apply fast mitigations; notify PM | 1 hour |
| 5–20%                 | 4–8x      | Apply medium mitigations; open bridge | 30 minutes |
| < 5%                  | >8x       | Conservative mitigations; Exec comms | 15 minutes |

Reliability Initiative Short Roster (run-critical items to reduce future burn)

- Short-term (2–6 weeks):
  - Implement per-tenant request shaping to prevent noisy neighbor storms. Owner: Platform Traffic Team.
  - Add predictive autoscale burst policy for nightly traffic spikes. Owner: SRE Capacity.

- Mid-term (6–16 weeks):
  - Extend prefix/KV cache coverage to top-1000 user prefixes and add telemetry to measure warm-up effectiveness. Owner: Serving Runtime.
  - Add synthetic SLO probes from multiple regions to detect regressions earlier. Owner: Observability.

Operational Tooling and Playbooks

- Playbook: Automated rollback guard rails
  - `deployctl guard status --service serving-runtime` to confirm guard rails before rollback.
  - Rollback must be accompanied by a POST to the incident timeline API:
    - `curl -X POST $INCIDENT_API/timeline -d '{"actor":"$USER","action":"rollback","reason":"..."}'`

- Playbook: Error budget ledger update (manual if automation fails)
  - Record the time window, SLO impact, estimated user-minutes lost. Use the ledger command: `slo-ledger record --service serving-runtime --window 2026-02-17T00:00:00Z/2026-02-17T01:00:00Z --impact 0.32`

Incident Review Standards and Handoff

- Post-incident required artifacts (to be submitted within 72 hours):
  1) Timeline of events with timestamps and owner at each step.
  2) Root cause hypothesis and evidence (logs, traces, kernel profile snippets).
  3) Decision lattice entry: which mitigations were attempted, in what order, and why.
  4) Error budget accounting: ledger entries pre/post incident.
  5) Remediation plan with owners and deadlines (targeted within 14 days).

- Review cadence:
  - Triage meeting within 5 business days to validate evidence.
  - Blameless review and remediation prioritization within 14 days.

Documenting mitigation rationale (example snippet)

- Example entry for timeline: 
  - 2026-02-17T09:12Z - Alert fired: p99 latency 320ms (SLO 200ms). PagerDuty triggered. Owner: oncall-sre-A.
  - 2026-02-17T09:18Z - Autoscale bump applied (+1 serving-gpu). No change.
  - 2026-02-17T09:30Z - Rollback to model v1 (previous stable). P99 dropped to 180ms. Action: retained.

Communication templates

- Internal oncall message (Slack):
  - `INCIDENT: serving-runtime p99 latency above SLO. Mitigation: rollback to v1 applied; monitoring for 1h. Timeline: https://redwood/inc/12345`

- Customer-facing template (when error budget exhausted or significant outage):
  - Subject: "Service interruption affecting model serving"
  - Body: "We experienced a partial outage of model-serving in region eu-west-1 between 09:12–09:45 UTC on 2026-02-17. We applied a rollback and restored service. We are investigating root cause and will provide a remediation plan within 14 days. If you need immediate assistance, contact your account team."

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary oncall: SRE rotation (pager: oncall-sre@redwood.com)
- Service owner: 
  - serving-runtime: team-serving-runtime@redwood.com (Owner: Derek Kim)
- Capacity lead: SRE Capacity (capacity-lead@redwood.com)
- Observability lead: telemetry@redwood.com

Appendix: Example queries and commands

- SLO probe query (PromQL):
  - `sum(rate(requests_total{service="serving-runtime",status!~"5.."}[30d])) / sum(rate(requests_total{service="serving-runtime"}[30d]))`

- Quick health check script (bash):
  - `#!/bin/bash
  set -e
  echo "Checking P99..."
  curl -s "https://observability/api/query?p99&service=serving-runtime"
  echo "Checking GPU pools..."
  infractl pool status --pool serving-gpu`
